chunks: (For) when his Lord said to him: "Obey," he replied: "I submit to the Lord of all the worlds."

key_terms.لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: To the Lord of all the worlds

ai.seo_question: What was Ibrahim's response when his Lord commanded him to submit?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as the archetype of immediate, unhesitating obedience (as-sam' wa al-ta'ah), contrasting Ibrahim's readiness with the hesitation of others. It establishes the etymological and spiritual root of 'Islam' not merely as ritual submission, but as a total surrender of the self to the Divine Will, a concept central to the Imamate's role as the perfect exemplar of this submission.
